method: Per-venue-class research workstreams, each independently searched and required to cite a fetched URL for every capacity figure and calendar URL. Compiled deterministically; identity reconciled conservatively; nothing admitted to any production registry.

workstreams.method_notes: Independent cross-check of two never-verified census populations (INDOOR_ARENA n=41; GREYHOUND_STADIUM n=18, all 18 capacity-review-flagged) plus the arena-adjacent sporting populations (ice hockey, basketball, athletics, tennis). Existing census venues were extracted programmatically from research/major-event-venues/uk-major-event-census-01/venues.json (642 venues; 41 INDOOR_ARENA, 18 GREYHOUND_STADIUM, 14 OTHER_SPORTS_VENUE) and every candidate below was name+city+alternative-name matched against the full 642 before being proposed, so nothing here is a known duplicate. REFERENCE POPULATIONS CHECKED: (1) National Arenas Association member list (fetched https://www.nationalarenasassociation.com/ - 23 members incl. one Irish); (2) Wikipedia List of indoor arenas in the United Kingdom (operational, under-construction and former sections); (3) Elite Ice Hockey League 2025-26 season venue list (10 venues); (4) Super League Basketball 2025-26 season venue list (9 venues); (5) Greyhound Board of Great Britain's own published licensed-track count (fetched https://www.gbgb.org.uk/racing/race-courses/ and https://www.gbgb.org.uk/rules-regulation/licensing/tracks/ - BOTH state 16 licensed stadia) cross-read against the named 16-track list and then confirmed track-by-track against each track's own official site; (6) UK greyhound openings/closures register maintained by the trade publication Greyhound Racing Times; (7) major permanent tennis tournament venues; (8) major athletics stadium population. VERDICT - INDOOR_ARENA: UNDERCOUNTED. The top-tier concert/entertainment arena estate is in fact substantially covered by the census as a whole - every NAA member arena except one, and every operational arena on the Wikipedia UK indoor arena list, reconciles to an existing census record - but several of them sit under a DIFFERENT venue_type and so are excluded from the 41 (P&J Live Aberdeen is CONVENTION_CENTRE; Brighton Centre, Swansea Building Society Arena, Alexandra Palace and Windsor Hall/Bournemouth are AUDITORIUM; Olympia London and The NEC are EXHIBITION_CENTRE; Royal Albert Hall is CONCERT_HALL; Emirates Arena Glasgow is OTHER_SPORTS_VENUE). Those are classification questions, not gaps, and are reported rather than re-listed here so as not to create duplicates. The REAL undercount is in the mid-scale (1,400-3,500 capacity) purpose-built sporting/entertainment arena tier: only 2 of the 9 Super League Basketball venues (Copper Box Arena, Playsport Arena) were in the census at all, and 1 of the 10 EIHL venues (Planet Ice Altrincham) was missing. Six operational arena-type venues and one under-construction arena are added below, plus one genuinely missing NAA member arena (East of England Arena, Peterborough) classified as MULTI_PURPOSE_EVENT_COMPLEX. VERDICT - GREYHOUND_STADIUM: MATERIALLY WRONG, NOT MERELY INCOMPLETE. GBGB itself states 16 licensed tracks; the census carries 18 active ones. Both surplus records are corrected below: Oxford Stadium closed on 3 April 2026 and is set CLOSED; Mildenhall Stadium's greyhound operation closed on 2 April 2026 while the site itself continues as a Spedeworth speedway/stock-car venue, so it is re-typed OTHER_SPORTS_VENUE and left OPERATIONAL rather than being falsely killed off or falsely preserved as an active track. All 18 existing greyhound records are re-listed (same canonical_name + city) because all 18 carried CAPACITY_REVIEW_REQUIRED and six carried no official URL at all; this pass supplies verified official URLs, addresses and fixture calendars. VERDICT - ICE HOCKEY: PLAUSIBLY_COMPLETE after one addition (9 of 10 EIHL venues already present). VERDICT - BASKETBALL: UNDERCOUNTED (5 of 9 top-tier venues added; 2 more fall below the 1,000 threshold and are excluded with cited figures). VERDICT - ATHLETICS: PLAUSIBLY_COMPLETE - Alexander Stadium, London Stadium, Manchester Regional Arena, Gateshead International Stadium, Crystal Palace NSC, Scotstoun Stadium, Cardiff International Sports Stadium and the indoor Emirates/Glasgow International Arena are all already in the census; no >=1,000 athletics venue was established as missing. VERDICT - TENNIS: UNDERCOUNTED BY ONE - AELTC, Queen's Club, Devonshire Park and Nottingham Tennis Centre were present; Edgbaston Priory Club (Lexus Birmingham Open) was not and is added. EXCLUSIONS ARE STATED EXPLICITLY in each excluded venue's absence and in the report: Surrey Sports Park (970), SGS College/WISE Arena Bristol (750) and Lee Valley Athletics Centre (500 permanent seats) are all below the 1,000 threshold; Dundonald International Ice Bowl is a public leisure ice rink and Belfast Giants training/secondary venue with no established spectator capacity; Edinburgh Arena at Edinburgh Park has planning consent but construction had NOT started as of July 2026, so no permitted operational_status honestly applies and it is deliberately omitted; the remaining Planet Ice community rinks (Blackburn, Bristol, Gillingham, Gosport, Hemel Hempstead, Leeds, Peterborough, Solihull, Uttoxeter, Widnes) were not evidenced as >=1,000 major-event infrastructure and are omitted. NO capacity, address, postcode, date or URL below is asserted without a URL that was actually fetched; where no figure was found the capacity is null with CAPACITY_REVIEW_REQUIRED rather than guessed. Latitude/longitude are null throughout by instruction.

TASK A - BUSINESS-EVENT CAPABILITY AT SPORT VENUES. Read the census venues.json programmatically and extracted the 531 records whose venue_type is RACECOURSE, FOOTBALL_STADIUM, RUGBY_STADIUM, CRICKET_GROUND, INDOOR_ARENA or MOTORSPORT_CIRCUIT, plus their canonical_name/city/alternative_names, as the Task A candidate pool. Because the census already holds 811 venues including the whole purpose-built conference/exhibition estate (ExCeL, Olympia London, The ICC Birmingham, Telford International Centre, Harrogate Convention Centre, Manchester Central, Scottish Event Campus, P&J Live, ICC Belfast, ICC Wales, Bournemouth International Centre, Brighton Centre and others), the gap this workstream addresses is specifically the business-event layer inside sport venues. Examined in depth: 30 sport venues - 8 racecourses (Cheltenham, Doncaster, Aintree, Sandown Park, Newbury, Epsom Downs, Ascot, York), 13 football stadiums (Wembley, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Emirates, Stamford Bridge, Old Trafford, Etihad, Anfield, St James' Park, Villa Park, Elland Road, Ashton Gate, London Stadium, Hampden Park, Principality Stadium), 3 rugby stadiums (Allianz Stadium Twickenham, Scottish Gas Murrayfield, Sandy Park) and 5 cricket grounds (Emirates Old Trafford, Lord's, The Kia Oval, Edgbaston, Trent Bridge). Representation: exactly ONE (A1) separate sub-venue record was created - The Centaur at Cheltenham Racecourse - because it is the only sport-venue business-event facility found that is separately named, separately marketed on its own web estate AND separately calendared with its own public what's-on of named forthcoming events. Every other venue is recorded as (A2) business-event capability against the parent, re-listed with the exact canonical_name and city from venues.json and with the principal capacity deliberately null + CAPACITY_REVIEW_REQUIRED so the parent's proven spectator capacity is not displaced. Two sport-venue conference complexes were checked and found ALREADY HELD as separate census records, so no new record was made: Silverstone International Conference and Exhibition Centre (already a sub-venue of Silverstone Circuit) and Coventry Building Society Arena (already a MULTI_PURPOSE_EVENT_COMPLEX parent with its Indoor Arena as a sub-venue; its 6,000 sqm exhibition halls therefore already sit inside the census). SCHEMA CAVEAT: the workstream record schema's venue_type enum has no CRICKET_GROUND value, although cricket grounds were in scope as Task A candidates. The five cricket-ground (A2) records therefore carry venue_type MULTI_PURPOSE_EVENT_COMPLEX as the closest allowed value, and each one states in scale_description that the census parent's type is CRICKET_GROUND and that this is not a reclassification claim. The compiler should not treat these as venue_type election evidence. CALENDAR FINDING (the hire-page distinction): of the 30 sport venues examined, only 7 publish a genuine listing of named forthcoming BUSINESS or non-sport events - The Centaur (Cheltenham), Doncaster Racecourse, Sandown Park, Aintree, Epsom Downs, Ascot and Sandy Park. All 7 are recorded with calendar_sources. The other 23 publish venue-hire marketing only: capacity charts, floor plans, room galleries and enquiry forms, with their public what's-on covering stadium-bowl sport and concerts that the census already captures. That is the expected and honest result - conference, exhibition and banqueting bookings at stadiums are overwhelmingly private corporate events that are never published - and each such record carries a no_public_calendar_reason instead of a fabricated calendar. No hire page, capacity chart or enquiry form was recorded as a calendar.  TASK B - SHOWGROUND ESTATE AUDIT. Established programmatically that the census already held 17 permanent agricultural-society showgrounds: South of England Event Centre (Ardingly), Westpoint Exeter (Devon County Showground), Great Yorkshire Events Centre (Harrogate), Trinity Park (Ipswich/Suffolk), NAEC Stoneleigh, Lincolnshire Showground, Kent Event Centre (Detling), Three Counties Showground (Malvern), Newark Showground, Norfolk Showground, East of England Arena and Events Centre (Peterborough), Royal Bath & West Showground, Staffordshire County Showground, Royal Cornwall Events Centre, Eikon Exhibition Centre / Balmoral Park (Royal Ulster), Royal Highland Centre (Ingliston) and Royal Welsh Showground (Builth Wells). ASAO NEGATIVE FINDING: ASAO does not publish a member directory of shows or showgrounds. asao.co.uk/members/ returns HTTP 404, and the live directory at asao.co.uk/organisations/ lists only 8 organisations on the page (Welsh Pony & Cob Society, British Show Jumping, NFYFC, National Sheep Association, North West Federation of Show Societies, Royal Agricultural Society of England, Royal Windsor Show and London International Horse Show, Yeovil Agricultural Society) - none of which is a showground census. Wikipedia has no "List of agricultural shows in the United Kingdom" article (HTTP 404). The estate therefore had to be enumerated society-by-society from Wikipedia's agricultural-show categories and then corroborated against each society's own site; there is no authoritative national register to check against, which is itself the central limit on any completeness claim here. ADDED: 14 permanent showgrounds absent from the census - England: Cheshire Showground (Tabley/Knutsford), Newbury Showground, Westmorland County Show Ground (Crooklands), The West Mid Showground (Shrewsbury), Hertfordshire County Showground (Redbourn), Driffield Showground, Bakewell Showground. Wales: The Anglesey Showground (Gwalchmai/Mona), Carmarthen Showground (Nantyci), Monmouthshire Showground, Haverfordwest Showground (Pembrokeshire). Scotland: Borders Events Centre (Springwood Park, Kelso), Mannsfield Showground (Black Isle, Muir of Ord), The Haughs (Turriff). Northern Ireland: nothing further qualified beyond Balmoral Park, already held. The single most significant miss was the Borders Events Centre at Kelso - a 1,000 sqm purpose-built function hall seating 1,000 theatre style on a 40-acre permanent showground, with a live public events calendar. It is the largest permanent agricultural-society events building in Scotland after the Royal Highland Centre. EXCLUDED with reasons: Essex County Showground, Great Leighs (converted to a racecourse in 2008, no longer a society showground); Weedon Park, Aylesbury (Bucks County Show - society-held show field, no venue-hire or events offer found); New Park, Brockenhurst (New Forest Show - permanent ground but the society publishes no venue-hire or year-round events offer); Stoke Park, Guildford (Surrey County Show - council public park); North Somerset Agricultural Society (no showground venue identity; the show is moving site in 2027); Dorset County Show, Dorchester (no showground name, operator or hire offer published); Dorset Show Ground at West Stour (a private family equestrian centre, not an agricultural society showground - not to be confused with the Dorset County Show); Moreton Show, Honiton Show and Turnpike Showground, Motcombe (permanent or society-owned but no year-round venue business published - Honiton in particular is a genuine borderline, a society-owned 140-acre site with a show-only web presence); Denbigh & Flint, Dumfries (show fields); Clogher Valley Show and Omagh Show / Tyrone Farming Society in Northern Ireland (permanent grounds but single annual shows with no hire offer or what's-on); Ballymena Showgrounds (a council football stadium, already in the census as such); Nantwich (Dorfold Hall), Northumberland County Show (Bywell), Cumberland Show (Carlisle Racecourse), Newport Show (Chetwynd Deer Park), Vale of Glamorgan (Fonmon Castle) and Tendring Hundred (Lawford) - all staged on rented estate or racecourse land with no persistent venue identity. UNRESOLVED / COULD NOT FETCH: Royal Lancashire Show (royallancashireshow.org.uk does not resolve - historically a moving show); Stithians Show, Cornwall (TLS handshake failure); Keith Show, Moray (no response); Yeovil Agricultural Society, an actual ASAO member, whose domain now resolves to an unrelated commercial site. Thainstone Centre, Inverurie was considered and set aside as a commercial livestock-mart/exhibition centre operated by ANM Group rather than an agricultural society showground, but it was not fetched. VERDICT ON THE SHOWGROUND ESTATE: with 17 already held plus 14 added, the census now carries 31 permanent UK showgrounds and I judge the estate PLAUSIBLE BUT NOT PROVEN COMPLETE. Every large first-tier county/royal showground I could identify from society sources is now present in England, Wales and Scotland, and Northern Ireland's single qualifying ground was already held. The remaining risk is concentrated in the second tier - county societies that own a permanent ground but market it only as a show site - where the inclusion boundary is genuinely a judgement call, and in the four sites above that could not be fetched at all. I did NOT establish completeness: no national register of showgrounds exists to check against, ASAO publishes no member list, and the enumeration therefore rests on society-by-society discovery which cannot be proved exhaustive. Scotland and Wales are the thinnest coverage and would repay a further pass.  EVIDENCE DISCIPLINE: every capacity, square-metre, acreage, address and postcode in this file was read on a page I fetched myself, and the exact URL is cited in capacity_source and/or evidence. Where a first-party page published no figure, the field is null rather than filled from a third-party directory - notably Carmarthen (official 52 acres, not the 100 acres third parties quote), Anglesey (official 136 acres, not 160) and Pembrokeshire (no official figures at all, so the widely quoted 60 acres and Pavilion 250/400 capacities are deliberately NOT recorded). Allianz Stadium Twickenham carries a first-party "over 7,000 sqm" total against a trade-body "12,000m2"; the first-party figure is recorded and the conflict is noted. Sites that block plain HTTP fetchers (unitedcounties.org returns 403, pembsshow.org returns malformed headers) and calendars delivered through cross-origin widgets (Driffield) were read in a real browser. Latitude and longitude are null throughout.

Breadth-first census of UK concert halls, theatres and auditoria with capacity >= 1,000 across all four nations, compiled 2026-09-20 from pages actually fetched in-session. Most capacities are GRADE_B (Wikipedia article wikitext retrieved via the MediaWiki API; the exact API URL fetched is cited as capacity_source), with GRADE_A first-party confirmation where a venue or operator site could be fetched (e.g. Usher Hall 2,200 from cultureedinburgh.com, Sheffield City Hall operator from sheffieldcityhall.co.uk). Roughly 22 candidate venues were verified to be under 1,000 and excluded: 19 West End houses (Ambassadors 444, Apollo 658, Arts 350, Criterion 588, Duchess 494, Fortune 432, Garrick 718, Gielgud 994, Harold Pinter 796, Lyric 915, Noel Coward 942, Playhouse 550, @sohoplace 602, St Martin’s 550, Theatre Royal Haymarket 888, Tom Stoppard 640, Trafalgar 630, Vaudeville 690, Wyndham’s 799) plus Eden Court Empire Theatre 840, Dundee Rep c.455 and Theatr Clwyd 570; numerous sub-1,000 studio/second spaces inside included complexes (Lilian Baylis 200, Sage Two 600, Barbican Pit 200, Lyttelton 890, Dorfman 400, Spa Theatre 675, Sheffield Memorial Hall 500 and others) are noted in capacity_configuration rather than listed separately. Known limitations: several official sites (royalalberthall.com, southbankcentre.co.uk, lwtheatres.co.uk, trafalgarentertainment.com) returned 403/404/bot-detection so no first-party evidence was obtained for them; capacities marked CAPACITY_REVIEW_REQUIRED are venues confirmed to exist on a fetched operator directory but whose size was not verified, and Theatre Royal Brighton in particular may prove sub-1,000 on review. St David’s Hall Cardiff is recorded with operational_status STATUS_REVIEW_REQUIRED rather than OPERATIONAL because the fetched Wikipedia article states it closed in September 2023 due to RAAC in the roof and was "not expected to reopen until 2026" — whether it has now reopened was not verified.

Every capacity figure, square-metre figure, address and URL recorded below was read from a page that was actually fetched during this research pass; figures that appeared only in search-engine result summaries were deliberately NOT recorded, and those fields are left null with capacity_confidence CAPACITY_REVIEW_REQUIRED. Official first-party venue sites were preferred (GRADE_A); no third-party venue-directory figures were used as a capacity source. Calendar sources were only recorded where a fetched page listed actual forthcoming NAMED events; venues whose only public page was a 'hire our venue' / event-types marketing page were given zero calendar_sources and a no_public_calendar_reason. Operators were recorded only where a fetched page stated them, so several are null rather than guessed.

Dedicated second-pass national census of UK major business-event infrastructure, run because the first pass admitted only 22 conference/convention/exhibition venues (10 CONVENTION_CENTRE + 12 EXHIBITION_CENTRE, and CONFERENCE_CENTRE zero times). METHOD: (1) The 642 existing census records in venues.json were read programmatically and reduced to a canonical_name+city+nation+venue_type index; every candidate below was checked against that index before research, so venues already carried by other workstreams (e.g. Winter Gardens Blackpool, Venue Cymru, Westpoint Exeter, Brangwyn Hall, Caird Hall, Glasgow Royal Concert Hall, Music Hall Aberdeen, Usher Hall, Ulster Hall, Millennium Forum, Donald Gordon Theatre, The Glasshouse International Centre for Music, Brighton Dome, St George's Hall Bradford, Butterworth Hall, Bolton Arena, Silverstone Circuit) were deliberately NOT re-listed. (2) POPULATIONS ACTUALLY CHECKED, deliberately overlapping and never treated as truth on their own: Association of Event Venues full member directory (aev.org.uk/about-us/venue-members, 56 records across 6 pages, fetched); London & Partners / London Convention Bureau conference-venues directory (conventionbureau.london, all 6 pages); Unique Venues of London full member list (uniquevenuesoflondon.co.uk); Convention Edinburgh / Meeting Edinburgh searchable venue directory (meetingedinburgh.com/venues, 114 records with Max Theatre / Reception / Banqueting columns); Glasgow Life venue-hire directory (glasgowlife.org.uk/venue-hire, 3 pages); VisitScotland Business Events (businessevents.visitscotland.com - venue directory path is 404; only the conferences-and-exhibitions inspiration page carries capacities); VisitAberdeenshire business events (business.visitabdn.com - names no venues, lead-capture only); Business Events Wales / Meet in Wales (meetinwales.com - /venues is 404 and the search is client-rendered, but individual product pages carry structured capacity fields); Visit Cardiff / Meet Cardiff (meetcardiff.com/venues and /highlights/ pages); Visit Belfast business events (visitbelfastbusiness.events - client-rendered, static HTML exposes only 4 featured listings and its sitemap contains no venue pages: a genuine unswept population); NewcastleGateshead Convention Bureau; the agricultural-society / county-showground estate reached venue-by-venue from official society sites; and the official venue websites themselves, which were the primary evidence source throughout. (3) EVIDENCE RULE APPLIED: every non-null capacity_value cites the exact URL fetched that states it. Where a venue publishes only floor area, or only standing figures, or nothing, that is recorded honestly rather than guessed - six records carry capacity_value null with CAPACITY_REVIEW_REQUIRED. No coordinates were guessed; latitude/longitude are null throughout. Addresses and postcodes appear only where a fetched page stated them. (4) CALENDAR RULE APPLIED: venue-hire pages, capacity charts and floor plans were NOT recorded as calendars. Only pages listing actual named forthcoming events were recorded, and events_currently_present is true only where named forthcoming events with dates were actually seen in the fetched page. (5) CONSISTENT EXCLUSION RULE: hotel-integrated ballrooms and function suites were excluded even at 1,000+ (InterContinental London - The O2 / Arora Ballroom 3,100 theatre; JW Marriott Grosvenor House Great Room 1,300 theatre; Novotel London West Champagne Suite 1,400 theatre; Hilton Birmingham Metropole; Celtic Manor Resort Caernarfon Suite 1,200 theatre; Macdonald Aviemore Resort Osprey Arena 1,150 theatre; Prestonfield Edinburgh 1,000 theatre). These are evidenced and named in the hand-back report so the census owner can reverse that judgement in one pass. (6) LIMITATION: the session's WebSearch budget (200 calls) was exhausted partway through, so later discovery was WebFetch-only, navigating from official sites. Several sites refused automated fetches entirely (c-h-w.com, eastsiderooms.com, qub.ac.uk, swansea.gov.uk, ulster.ac.uk, visitpeterborough.com, cardiff.ac.uk) - where a figure could still be obtained it is marked with its real source grade, and where it could not, the gap is stated rather than filled.

Breadth-first census built entirely from pages fetched during this task: four Wikipedia stadium lists (England, Scotland, Wales-by-capacity, Northern Ireland) plus the 2026-27 Cymru Premier and NIFL Premiership club/ground tables were downloaded as rendered HTML and parsed mechanically (rowspans resolved, capacity templates expanded), so every name, capacity and city here was read from a real table cell rather than recalled. Coordinates, street addresses and official-website URLs came from the Wikidata API keyed on those articles' enwiki titles; 407 resulting official club/venue homepages were then fetched (357 returned 200) and every calendar URL recorded below was extracted from that fetched HTML, never guessed, then itself fetched (355 of 360 returned 200). Manchester City refused the bulk probe with HTTP 403 and was re-fetched by hand, so the Etihad Stadium entry is evidenced the same way as the rest. Coverage: all four nations, the top four English tiers plus National League/North/South grounds above ~5,000, every Scottish ground at or above 1,000, all NIFL Premiership and Cymru Premier grounds, and the national stadiums. Limitations to read honestly: capacity is almost entirely GRADE_C (Wikipedia tables, sometimes corroborated by Wikidata P1083) because the official club and stadium pages checked - Wembley, Hampden, Windsor Park, Old Trafford, Spurs, Etihad, Emirates, Ibrox, Wrexham - publish no capacity figure in fetchable HTML; only Swansea.com Stadium yielded a GRADE_A official figure. Where two fetched sources disagree (notably NIFL's current licensed capacities vs the NI stadium list) the current-season club table was preferred and the conflict is recorded with capacity_confidence LOW. events_currently_present is a mechanical signal (schema.org Event blocks or date-like strings in the fetched HTML), left null where a page returned 200 but was client-rendered. Murrayfield Stadium and Kingston Park appear in football-stadium source lists but were excluded because every tenant evidenced is a rugby organisation; Principality Stadium is included because the brief names it, flagged in its evidence as having no football use evidenced. Non-football venues in the Welsh general stadium list (rugby, cricket, ice hockey) were excluded. Only "Current stadiums" sections were used, so no closed or under-construction grounds are listed.

Breadth-first census of UK indoor arenas with capacity >= 1,000 across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, compiled 2026-09-20 from live WebSearch/WebFetch only. Population was seeded from the Wikipedia 'List of indoor arenas in the United Kingdom' (which only covers >= 5,000) and then extended downward using the Elite Ice Hockey League arena table, Planet Ice / council leisure operators, and convention-centre operators to reach the 1,000-9,999 band. Capacity figures are graded honestly: GRADE_A means the figure was read off a page on the venue's or operator's own site that I fetched; GRADE_C means a Wikipedia infobox or a WebSearch result summary. Where two sources disagree (common, because arenas have concert / sport / half-house configurations) the principal figure is in `capacity` and the rest in `additional_capacities`, with the conflict noted; where nothing could be verified the capacity is null and flagged CAPACITY_REVIEW_REQUIRED. Every URL in this file was returned by a search or fetch performed in this session - none are recalled from memory. This is research only: no source registry or public data was touched.

Targeted sweep of Northern Ireland's non-sport >=1,000-capacity major-event estate, closing the gap left by the earlier NI pass (which reached only 3 theatre/concert venues and 1 conference/exhibition venue for the whole nation). POPULATIONS WORKED THROUGH: (1) Visit Belfast business-events venue directory (https://www.visitbelfastbusiness.events/venues/) - CONFIRMED BLOCKED: the page ships only 4 'featured' listings in server HTML and loads the rest from a Simpleview rest_v2 endpoint (/includes/rest_v2/plugins_listings_listings/find/) that returns 403 'Invalid credentials' without a runtime-generated simpleToken; its sitemap.xml contains no /listing/ URLs. WORKED ROUND by (a) rendering the page in a headless browser, which surfaced ~20 listing names (Galgorm, Game of Thrones Studio Tour, Hastings Europa Hotel, Titanic Belfast, Custom House Belfast, Hilton Belfast, Ulster Transport Museum, Stormont Estate, St Comgall's, 2 Royal Avenue, Bullitt Hotel, Dunadry Hotel, W5 Belfast, Ulster Museum, Ten Square Hotel, Ulster Rugby, Belfast Cathedral, Maldron Hotel, Quintin Castle) - all hotels or attractions, none a non-sport >=1,000 event auditorium not already held; and (b) going to the operators, councils, universities and venues' own sites directly. (2) Tourism NI: discovernorthernireland.com/business-events resolves to a travel-trade page with no venue finder (the business-events venue paths the previous pass hit are still dead), but its THEATRES directory (https://discovernorthernireland.com/things-to-do/arts-culture-and-heritage/theatres/) IS server-rendered and enumerates the national theatre estate: Lyric, Grand Opera House, Waterfront Hall, Theatre at the Mill, Market Place Theatre Armagh, Alley Arts Centre Strabane, Strule Arts Centre Omagh, Ardhowen Theatre Enniskillen, Millennium Forum. Only Grand Opera House (1,058), Waterfront/ICC (2,000-2,250) and Millennium Forum (1,000) clear 1,000 - all three already in the census. (3) Belfast City Council: Ulster Hall and ICC Belfast (BWUH Ltd) already held; City Hall, 2 Royal Avenue and the community-centre estate are sub-1,000; the Council's own Licensing Committee papers were used as GRADE_A evidence for Boucher Road Playing Fields. (4) Derry City & Strabane: Guildhall Main Hall evidenced at 400 seated / 600 standing (sub-1,000, excluded); Millennium Forum already held; St Columb's Hall evidenced at 700 seats in current use (sub-1,000, excluded). (5) Armagh City Banbridge & Craigavon, Causeway Coast & Glens, Mid Ulster, Ards & North Down council hire estates fetched - all community centres and town halls, nothing approaching 1,000. (6) Fermanagh & Omagh: Ardhowen and Strule are sub-1,000; Fermanagh Lakeland Forum is a leisure centre, closed for redevelopment. (7) Queen's University Belfast events estate fetched in full: Whitla Hall 1,200 theatre (already held), Elmwood Hall 478, Great Hall 150, Isdell Courtyard 290, Riddel Hall rooms 276 - nothing else clears 1,000. Ulster University's largest lecture theatres are 400. (8) Royal Ulster Agricultural Society: Balmoral Park / Eikon Exhibition Centre already held (enriched here with the official 10,600 sqm figure); its predecessor the King's Hall is added as CLOSED. (9) Major NI entertainment venues via the Wikipedia UK venue list and promoter/venue sites. JUDGEMENT ON THE TRUE NI ESTATE: Northern Ireland genuinely has a small non-sport >=1,000 estate. The honest indoor list is roughly thirteen buildings: The O2 Belfast (11,200), ICC Belfast/Waterfront (2,000-2,250), Ulster Hall (1,850 standing), Sir William Whitla Hall (1,200), The Telegraph Building (1,200), Grand Opera House (1,058), Millennium Forum (1,000), Assembly Buildings Conference Centre (1,000), Eikon Exhibition Centre (10,600 sqm), Green Pastures Ballymena (1,600 auditorium), Whitewell Metropolitan Tabernacle (c.3,000 sanctuary), plus two now-closed buildings, King's Hall and the Titanic Exhibition Centre. Eight of those were already in the census; this workstream adds the remaining five plus three Belfast outdoor major-event sites. CATEGORY-BOUNDARY DECISIONS, stated so the census owner can override them: (a) HOTELS ARE EXCLUDED, because the brief's scope list does not include them and no hotel appears anywhere in the existing 811-venue census; several NI hotels do market 1,000+ conference/banqueting capacity (Hastings Europa c.1,200 gala, Crowne Plaza Belfast up to 1,000, La Mon Hotel up to 1,000) and would materially change the NI conference count if the census owner wants them in. (b) OUTDOOR CONCERT SITES ARE INCLUDED here as OTHER_MAJOR_EVENT_VENUE (Custom House Square, Ormeau Park, Boucher Road Playing Fields) even though the existing census contains no outdoor non-sport venue anywhere in GB - these are demonstrably among NI's largest event sites and omitting them silently would misdescribe the nation; flagged for review. (c) LARGE CHURCH AUDITORIA ARE INCLUDED (Green Pastures Ballymena, Whitewell Metropolitan Tabernacle) because they are the only non-sport auditoria over 1,000 seats in their districts; both are flagged, and Whitewell carries a null capacity because the only figure found is a 2010 third-party description. NOT ESTABLISHED / STILL OPEN: Stormont Estate, Titanic Slipways and Ebrington Square (Derry) all host large outdoor events but no capacity figure was found on any page fetched, so none is recorded; a licensed-capacity source (council entertainments-licence register) would settle them and Belfast City Council does not publish one online.

Targeted national pass for UK performance venues with capacity >= 1,000, run 2026-09-20 against the existing 642-venue census. RECONCILIATION: research/major-event-venues/uk-major-event-census-01/venues.json was parsed programmatically (never eyeballed) and every existing canonical_name + alternative_names + city combination was extracted before any candidate was written. The file grew from 642 to 676 records while this pass was running, so the de-duplication was re-run against the final 676-record state across ALL venue_types (not just performance types) using normalised name matching that strips punctuation, case and a leading definite article. === METHOD/TOOLING LIMITS ===
Every capacity, address, postcode and calendar claim in this file cites a URL that was actually fetched; where a fact could not be established it is recorded as null with the absence itself evidenced, rather than guessed. OpenStreetMap was NOT used for completeness anywhere. The session's web-search budget (200 calls) was exhausted partway through, after which enumeration relied on direct fetches of known governing-body, league and operator URLs; this limited discovery of venues for which no candidate URL was already held, and is the main reason the residual gaps above remain open.

Targeted closure of the Welsh non-sport gap in the UK major-event census (census previously held 65 Welsh venues, of which only 8 theatre/concert/auditorium and 1 conference/exhibition). Scope: Wales, >=1,000 capacity, NON-SPORT only. Existing census name+city pairs and alternative_names were extracted programmatically from venues.json before research began, and the four records here that re-use an existing canonical_name+city (Venue Cymru/Llandudno, Rhyl Pavilion Theatre/Rhyl, Royal Welsh Showground/Builth Wells, St David's Hall/Cardiff) are deliberate enrichments of records that previously carried capacity_value null and, in the case of St David's Hall, operational_status STATUS_REVIEW_REQUIRED. POPULATIONS CHECKED: all 22 Welsh council areas were worked through by name for non-sport venues of >=1,000 capacity; Business Events Wales / Meet in Wales (meetinwales.com) including its association-venue-capacity page and the North Wales regional pages; meetnorthwales.co.uk large-conference venue listing; Visit Wales / Visit Mid Wales / Show Me Wales destination directories; Denbighshire Leisure Ltd's event-venue estate; Wrexham University, Bangor University, Aberystwyth University, Swansea University and UWTSD Carmarthen commercial/venue estates; ATG (Swansea Arena, held), Academy Music Group (St David's Hall lease), Live Nation (new Cardiff Bay Arena) and Depot Live (Cardiff Castle, Blackweir) operator portfolios; the Royal Welsh Agricultural Society showground plus the Anglesey, Carmarthen (United Counties/Nantyci), Pembrokeshire (Withybush) and Denbigh & Flint showgrounds. DELIBERATE GEOGRAPHIC EMPHASIS: research started in North, Mid and West Wales rather than Cardiff. Of the 17 records here, 6 are North Wales (Wrexham, Llangollen, Rhyl x2, Llandudno, Anglesey), 2 Mid Wales (Aberystwyth, Builth Wells), 3 West Wales (Llanelli, Carmarthen, Haverfordwest) and 6 South-East Wales (Newport x2, Cardiff x4) - i.e. a majority outside the south-east. No geographic quota was imposed; this reflects what the evidence showed. ACCESS OBSTACLES AND ESCALATION: Business Events Wales /venues 404s and its search is client-rendered, so discovery went via councils, operator portfolios, universities and venues' own sites. Plain unauthenticated fetches (Level 1) were tried first throughout; aberystwythartscentre.co.uk and unitedcounties.org returned 403/blocked to a plain fetch and were then opened in a real browser (Level 3) to read the same public pages, which is how the Great Hall capacity and the Carmarthen Showground hire/what's-on facts were obtained. llanellitowncouncil.gov.uk returned a 403 'Security Check' to both a plain fetch and a browser session; that boundary was respected and not worked around, so the Selwyn Samuel Centre capacity is cited to a GRADE_B directory instead and its calendar is recorded as unestablished. cardiff.gov.uk, seetickets.com, showmewales.co.uk (partially) and celtic-manor PDF extraction were also unavailable; where that left a fact unproven it is recorded as unproven, not guessed. EXCLUSIONS - checked and rejected as genuinely sub-1,000, each with a cited figure: Theatr Clwyd, Mold - Anthony Hopkins Theatre 569 seats (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theatr_Clwyd); Pontio, Bangor - Theatr Bryn Terfel 480 seats (pontio.co.uk/en/your-visit/the-centre); Princess Royal Theatre, Port Talbot - 798 (cvent venue page); Swansea University Great Hall, Bay Campus - 700-seat Sir Stanley Clarke Auditorium (conferencesandevents.swansea.ac.uk); Cardiff City Hall - Assembly Room 600 theatre-style, its largest room (cardiffcityhall.com/rooms/assembly-room/); The Vale Resort, Hensol - Castle Suite 700 theatre-style, its largest (valeresort.com/our-spaces/); Prichard-Jones Hall, Bangor University - 240 (bangor.ac.uk/weddings/venues); Halliwell Centre, Carmarthen (UWTSD) - theatre 325, main conference suite 200 (venuewales.co.uk); Grand Pavilion, Porthcawl - 643 (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Pavilion,_Porthcawl); Y Stiwt, Rhosllanerchrugog - 490 seats (stiwt.com / Theatres Trust); Ffwrnes, Llanelli - 504 main auditorium (theatrausirgar.co.uk); Coal Exchange, Cardiff - Grand Hall Suite 800 reception / 400 theatre, its largest (coalexchangecardiff.co.uk/grand-hall-suite/). Also checked and left out for want of any evidenced >=1,000 event space or any capacity evidence at all: Pontins Prestatyn Sands (holiday park, closed with immediate effect 30 November 2023 - no capacity figure for its entertainment venue could be evidenced, so it is not recorded as a venue); Margam Country Park, Neath Port Talbot (hosts the In It Together festival and outdoor cinema but no capacity figure could be evidenced); Denbigh & Flint Show ground at The Green, Denbigh, Vale of Glamorgan Show at Fonmon and the Monmouthshire Show at Vauxhall Fields (annual one-day shows on fields rather than standing hireable showgrounds, and no first-party capacity); Singleton Park, Swansea. JUDGEMENT ON THE TRUE WELSH ESTATE: the previous pass's instinct was right - the genuine Welsh non-sport >=1,000 estate is small, and this pass has now evidenced why rather than assumed it. Outside Cardiff, Swansea and Newport, Wales has very few permanent indoor venues over 1,000: the North Wales estate above that line is essentially Venue Cymru, Rhyl Pavilion, Rhyl Events Arena, William Aston Hall and the Royal International Pavilion; Mid Wales is Aberystwyth Arts Centre and the Royal Welsh Showground; West Wales is the Selwyn Samuel Centre plus two county showgrounds. Every other significant Welsh theatre and arts centre checked in Gwynedd, Conwy, Denbighshire, Flintshire, Wrexham, Anglesey, Powys, Ceredigion, Pembrokeshire, Carmarthenshire, RCT, Caerphilly, Torfaen, Blaenau Gwent, Merthyr, Bridgend, Monmouthshire, Neath Port Talbot and the Vale of Glamorgan sits in the 250-800 seat band. This is not a claim of completeness: the county-showground population and outdoor/greenfield concert sites remain only partially evidenced (three of the four showgrounds here carry no proven capacity number), and no systematic sweep of hotel ballrooms or university lecture-theatre complexes was performed beyond the largest candidates named above.
